source: Daily Investment Brief Macroeconomic Dashboard + authoritative-source supplementation
sourceStatus: Daily Investment Brief remains the primary dashboard layer, but automated retrieval still exposes client-side placeholders ('Analyzing...' / '--'). No values are inferred from placeholders. MacroMicro remains supplemental where accessible. Current gaps are filled with official ISM/FRED/Federal Reserve/EIA evidence plus current Reuters/market reporting. The retired legacy macro dashboard is not used.
methodology: Directional channels are scored from -2 to +2. Dashboard readings are inputs, not trading signals. Creator/video/social claims have zero direct score weight until independently verified. Company-specific evidence can strengthen a category without mechanically changing holding fundamental scores.
regime: Stagflationary services reacceleration inside a bifurcated economy: August services activity/orders accelerated sharply while prices rose to a four-year extreme and employment stayed contractionary. Physical AI/power capex remains strong; refined-product inflation is extreme. Waller-driven rate relief improved risk appetite and precious metals tactically, but long/real yields remain structurally restrictive.

channels.label: Growth / Demand
channels.regime: Services reaccelerating; manufacturing still expansionary; hiring weak
channels.interpretation: August Services 55.4, Business Activity 61.7 and New Orders 60.9 materially improve current-demand evidence. Manufacturing remains expansionary at 54.6. The offset is weak services employment, so this is demand reacceleration without a broad labour boom.

channels.label: Policy Relief
channels.regime: Near-term hike risk eased, inflation constraint remains
channels.interpretation: Waller's willingness to hold rates steady if inflation moderates cut September hike odds toward 54%. Services Prices at 72.6 and record diesel prevent a clean dovish regime shift.

channels.label: Financial Conditions
channels.regime: Tactical yield relief inside structurally restrictive long-rate regime
channels.interpretation: The US 10Y eased toward 4.77%, supporting equities and gold, but mortgage rates near 6.71% and structurally high real/long yields keep duration and leveraged projects expensive.

channels.label: Broad Credit
channels.regime: Open for quality, expensive for marginal borrowers
channels.interpretation: Large quality issuers can finance capex, but elevated risk-free rates keep funding quality, deposits and cash conversion important.

channels.label: Weak-End Credit Stress
channels.interpretation: The prior ~14.6% CCC reference remains punitive. Do not treat one day of equity/rate relief as a refinancing reset for weak borrowers.

channels.label: Consumer
channels.regime: Services spending resilient, affordability still squeezed
channels.interpretation: Strong services orders/activity show consumers/businesses are still spending, but record diesel, high mortgages and soft hiring continue to pressure financed discretionary demand.

channels.label: Housing
channels.interpretation: Mortgage rates around 6.71% remain a direct headwind to housing turnover and leveraged construction despite a modest Treasury-yield pullback.

channels.label: Industrial / AI / Power Capex
channels.interpretation: Official ISM Services comments explicitly link large transmission/generation investment to material purchasing, head count and long-lead planning. This adds survey confirmation to the already-verified AI server, memory, networking and power backlog evidence.

channels.label: AI Memory / Bandwidth
channels.regime: Constrained supply and capacity reallocation toward next-gen AI
channels.interpretation: Manufacturing still reports memory/electronic components in short supply, while Services comments indicate supplier capacity is shifting toward next-generation AI silicon. Near-term scarcity remains strong; future supply response remains the main cycle risk.

channels.label: Input Costs
channels.regime: Services and industrial cost inflation extreme
channels.interpretation: Services Prices rose to 72.6; Manufacturing Prices remain 71.1; record diesel plus metals/electronics/memory constraints keep input-cost pressure at the top of the scale.

channels.label: Labour
channels.interpretation: Services Employment at 47.8 remains contractionary even as activity/orders accelerate. NFP is the next major test and is not pre-empted.

channels.label: Risk Appetite
channels.interpretation: S&P +1.1% and Nasdaq +1.4% with software/Big Tech leadership show a meaningful tactical improvement. Keep it below full risk-on because inflation, oil and long-rate risks remain unresolved.

channels.label: Crude
channels.interpretation: Brent ~$95.52 and WTI ~$91.30 remain elevated. Escalation risk is offset by potential Russia-Ukraine peace progress and demand-destruction risk.

channels.label: Refined Products
channels.interpretation: US diesel retail and diesel cracks reached records while inventories remain historically low. This is the strongest current energy-inflation channel.

channels.label: US Gas / Global LNG
channels.interpretation: Energy-security diversification continues to support contracted US LNG infrastructure; exact spot-gas dashboard values were not refreshed from an authoritative source this run.

channels.label: Gold / Monetary Hedge
channels.regime: Tactical confirmation within structural hedge thesis
channels.interpretation: Gold +2.3%, silver +2.8% and broader precious-metal strength after Waller/yield relief materially improve tactical confirmation. NFP/CPI and real yields remain the key invalidation tests.
